finish.summary: Built triangular 3-base cluster with mount spike at shared junction carrying large platform accessory, forming a display stand. Capped open faces and locked joints, mesh clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your display stand — I'll set it on a spike-mounted large platform at the three-base junction.

2 part(s) could slide apart (2 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.

offersNear.note: Open offers at the base just added (valid until the next change): apply one by its socket, no find_sockets needed.

events.text: Three bases are in place at that junction — now I'll add the spiked large platform.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

outcomes.message: a solid spike cannot carry a platform; only a mount spike can: details.steps fits a mount spike on the same junction, then the platform.
a solid spike cannot carry a platform; only a mount spike can: details.steps fits a mount spike on the same junction, then the platform.

events.text: The display platform is mounted — I'll now run the final checks to complete it.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.
